Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct the FIRST attached native 1254 x 1254 game-art crop, at exactly the same 1254 x 1254 output size and original framing. Image 2 is a native-size locator detail of the defect, not the output target. Last three attachments are approved layout/material/style references only. All content outside the first image is not to be copied into the scene.
Keep all existing forms, their original positions, scale, perspective, daylight and painting style. No added objects. The outer 115-pixel border of the full target is immutable context. Make the fixed object meet every outer entry boundary exactly. No rescaling, stretching, blur, blending, sharpening or replacement scene.
Repair the full wooden dock railing assembly crossing the false vertical image join at target x=627. Both the UPPER and LOWER parallel diagonal beams have accidental steps at that x coordinate; the lower one drops 11 pixels at y~615, the upper one also kinks near y~100 and y~250. The turquoise water has an artificial straight tone boundary along the same x. These are source seams, NOT carpentry joints or notches. Restore BOTH beams as continuous single straight pieces, preserving their anchored endpoints at left and right, their consistent thickness, highlight, wood grain and their parallel perspective. Keep all three real vertical pickets exactly at their existing positions and sizes; keep their joints physically attached to both continuous beams. The middle picket near x627 must not be duplicated or deleted.
The lower deck rim near y1060 also has a small cut at x627; continue it as a single straight edge with unchanged endpoints. Restore continuous water texture and color across the false vertical source boundary. No new joints, cover strips, boards, objects or ornaments. Preserve all original paving above, posts, gold finial, deck and all outside 115-pixel borders. This is a whole-object join repair with both horizontal rails, all three pickets, water backdrop and lower deck entry geometry present, not a narrow seam band. The close locator focuses the most obvious lower-rail error; the full target shows all parallel elements. Output 1254 x 1254 at unchanged native scale.
